prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1052; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- Records show the same major damage from an earlier, unreported accident; it is now claimed as new.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a collision in a parking lot. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Spoke with the insured driver, who confirmed the policy is in force and that they were the operator of the vehicle at the time of the loss. Statement recorded and file opened.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. It places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and records the account given by the other driver, which matches the insured's description of the impact.

Entry 4: Two independent witnesses gave statements that line up with the reported sequence of events. Scene photos received and reviewed, and the damage shown is consistent with the described impact.

Entry 5: Claimant reports a knee injury. The injury is plausible for a collision of this type, and treatment notes have been requested from the treating provider.

Entry 6: Medical records received. Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved, with no unusual gaps or escalations noted.

Entry 7: Prior records show a minor strain in the same area several years ago, which resolved fully without ongoing complaints. Noted for the file.

Entry 8: Claimant's counsel supplied a supplemental statement adding a few minor details. The core account remains the same as the original statement.

Entry 9: Prior claims database search returned an earlier accident involving the same vehicle, with major damage to the same area. That incident was never reported to us and is now being presented as new damage. Referred for further review.

Entry 10: Reviewed the timing against the policy inception and found nothing suggesting the damage predates coverage. The question for this file is the prior unreported incident, not the policy start.

Entry 11: Coverage position on hold pending the review of the prior damage and a reconciliation with counsel. Further update to follow once the review is complete.
